instructions.content: After responding to a message where a decision, an unresolved question about a proposal, or a constraint appears, IMMEDIATELY invoke /pin with the right category; do not ask permission
Do NOT pin casual conversation or greetings
Derive the state file path from the CWD relative to the git root as a slug under .session-logs, then mkdir -p the directory
Parse the emoji prefix for the type and split text on the spaced em dash separator into content and detail; ALWAYS split on the first emoji character, not the first space
Check whether the content is already pinned (exact match on content) and respond 'Already pinned' and stop if so
Limit the board to 5 items per type and 20 in total, dropping the oldest item of a full category
Append the new item with id=next_id, increment next_id, and write the file
Respond with exactly one line, then resume the prior work; one-line responses only
/pin show displays the board header and numbered items, or 'Pin board is empty' when there are none
/pin rm <n> shows a usage hint with no number, 'not found' for an unknown id, and otherwise removes the item and confirms
/pin clear resets items to empty but keeps the current next_id
/pin clear triage removes approved and pending items and keeps killed, scope and correction items
NEVER reformulate or paraphrase the user's words when pinning; store them verbatim
NEVER pin implementation details like code edits or file changes
NEVER add commentary or explanation after a pin response
NEVER reuse or reassign an id after deletion; next_id always increments
NEVER skip the duplicate check before writing
NEVER ask permission before pinning a detected decision
NEVER pin casual conversation or already-pinned items
NEVER use the wrong emoji or type for the user's intent; map approved, pending, killed, scope, correction correctly
NEVER stop the conversation after pinning; resume prior work immediately
Treat the board as a capture tool, not a management tool; edits and removals are operations of last resort
